sentences: Measured on an AMD Radeon RX 6800 (gfx1030, not the console's gfx1013) with the hw-oracle tool from the AnyPS5 project, 537 input rows in all four IEEE/DX10_CLAMP combinations and in wave32 and wave64, the same for every combination with quiet NaNs.
`v_min_f32`/`v_max_f32`, `v_min_f16`/`v_max_f16` and each half of `v_pk_min_f16`/`v_pk_max_f16`: one NaN operand gives the other operand, bits unchanged; both NaN give src0; -0 < +0.
`v_min3`/`v_max3` = f(f(s0, s1), s2) with that min/max.
`v_med3_f32`/`_f16`: with any NaN operand the result is min3(s0, s1, s2), otherwise the median (-0 < +0).

`v_fract_f32` rounds x − floor(x) once and returns 0x3f7fffff (the largest float below 1) where that gives 1.0, e.g. fract(-1e-10); f16 gives 0x3bff; fract(-0) = +0, fract(±inf) = NaN, a NaN passes through.

Measured natively on gfx1036 (RDNA2) in the MODE inferred for the game (IEEE 0, f32 denormals flushed): `v_floor_f32`, `v_ceil_f32` and `v_fract_f32` read a denormal operand as a zero of its sign (floor(-1e-45) = -0, ceil(+1e-45) = +0, fract of either 0), fract(±inf) is exactly `0xffc00000`, and a NaN operand comes back unchanged, a signalling one too.

The translator flushes the operand and selects those words itself (`Gen.round_f32_flushed`) instead of leaving them to the driver's f32 denormal handling, which Vulkan does not fix; until 2026-11-22 a driver that keeps denormals gave -1.0, +1.0 and 0x3f7fffff there.
`v_cvt_flr_i32_f32` likewise returns 0 for a negative denormal (the translator gave -1).
Checked against 119 measured words by `tests/semantic/test_alu_floor_ceil_fract_hw.py`.
For `v_fract_f16`, either infinity gives the gfx1036 word `0xfe00`, or +0 with the DX10 clamp.
The translator selects these results explicitly.

The hand-written `ps_fract_f16_infinity.asm` fixture checks both signs, the preserved destination bits and a color channel computed from the result sign in the CPU interpreter (`tests/semantic/test_fract_f16_infinity.py`).
A source `neg` on a signalling NaN operand still quiets it in the translator.
Not changed: f16 fract(±inf) is `0xfe00` on the hardware and a quiet positive NaN in the translator, and `neg` on a signalling NaN operand quiets it in the translator.

The translator emits `NMin`/`NMax` for these min/max ops (before: `FMin`/`FMax`, whose NaN result GLSL.std.450 leaves to the implementation). med3 is `NMin(NMax(z, NMin(x, y)), NMax(x, y))` (until 2026-11-22 this used `FClamp(z, lo, hi)`, which was GLSL.std.450 undefined whenever `z` was NaN or both `x` and `y` were NaN), and when an operand can be a NaN, `OpIsNan` of each such operand (none for an inline or literal constant that is not a NaN) selects `NMin(NMin(x, y), z)` instead; all 1-, 2-, and 3-NaN operand positions for both `v_med3_f32` and `v_med3_f16` were hardware-verified on RDNA2 (`gfx1035`, wave32 & wave64).

`FMin`/`FMax`, whose NaN result GLSL.std.450 leaves to the implementation). med3 is `FClamp(z, NMin(x, y), NMax(x, y))`, and when an operand can be a NaN, `OpIsNan` of each such operand (none for an inline or literal constant that is not a NaN) selects `NMin(NMin(x, y), z)` instead.

`v_fract_f32` is `Fract` followed by `OpFOrdEqual` with 1.0 and an `OpSelect` of 0x3f7fffff, so the NaN of fract(±inf) is kept; `v_fract_f16` does the same before packing and then replaces a packed 0x3c00 with 0x3bff (not after an output multiplier, where 1.0 can be a true result).
Other `FMin`/`FMax`/`FClamp` uses (the `clamp` bit, LOD and conversion clamps, `v_cvt_pk_u8_f32`, the BVH slab test) are unchanged.

Not modelled: signalling NaNs under IEEE mode; NaN under the `clamp` bit (hardware gives +0 with DX10_CLAMP=1 and the NaN with DX10_CLAMP=0; the translator still emits `FClamp`); the payload when all operands are NaN in the f16 or three-source forms (`NMin` and `NMax` only promise a NaN).

The binary `v_min_f32` and `v_max_f32` forms explicitly select the first operand when the second is NaN, preserving the first quiet NaN's sign and payload when both are quiet NaNs, as measured on the RX 6800.
The CPU test `tests/semantic/test_minmax_f32_payload.py` checks both operand orders using finite color exports.
Also, without the `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve` execution mode Vulkan does not strictly guarantee NaN or signed-zero behaviour, so these rules hold where the driver keeps them.

NaN under the `clamp` bit (hardware gives +0 with DX10_CLAMP=1 and the NaN with DX10_CLAMP=0; the translator still emits `FClamp`); the NaN payload when both operands are NaN (`NMin` only promises a NaN); and without the `SignedZeroInfNanPreserve` execution mode Vulkan does not strictly guarantee NaN or signed-zero behaviour, so these rules hold where the driver keeps them.

With an output modifier (`mul:2`, `mul:4`, `div:2`) on `v_fract_f16` the translator applies the modifier to the f32 fract before narrowing to f16; the hardware order of rounding and modifier for that case was not measured, so a result can differ by one f16 step for tiny negative inputs (e.g. x = -1e-4 with `div:2`).

GPU-checked with `runtime/test/shaders/ps_fnan_med3.asm` and `ps_fnan_fract.asm` (inputs read from memory at run time) on an AMD Radeon RX 6800, Windows 11, driver 26.11.2: 4096/4096 pixels exact; on that driver the two med3 words differed before the change (0x40e00000 and 0x40600000 instead of 0x40a00000 and 0xc0200000), and so did the f16 fract word (0x3c00 instead of 0x3bff) once f16 results were narrowed with integer round-to-nearest; the f32 fract and the min/max words were already the hardware words there.
`tests/semantic/test_float_nan_fract.py` runs the measured rows through the translator and the interpreter.
